questions.question: What is a service?
questions.answer: A service encapsulates reusable logic or state and can be injected where needed.
questions.example: UserService owns API access instead of putting HTTP calls in every component.
questions.followup: When should state stay inside a component?

questions.question: Reactive forms vs template-driven forms?
questions.answer: Reactive forms define form state and validation in TypeScript; template-driven forms rely more on template directives.
questions.example: Complex dynamic validation is usually easier to model with reactive forms.
questions.followup: What is the benefit for testing?

questions.question: setValue vs patchValue?
questions.answer: setValue expects the complete form structure; patchValue updates only supplied controls.
questions.example: Patch a single profile field without supplying every form control.
questions.followup: When would setValue be useful as a safety check?

questions.question: Explain OnPush.
questions.answer: OnPush allows Angular to skip a component subtree until relevant notifications occur, such as input reference changes, events, reactive updates or explicit marking.
questions.example: Replacing items with a new array works; mutating the same array reference can produce stale UI.
questions.followup: How would you diagnose a stale OnPush view?

questions.question: switchMap vs mergeMap?
questions.answer: switchMap cancels the previous inner subscription when new input arrives; mergeMap allows concurrent inner work.
questions.example: Use switchMap for typeahead search; use mergeMap when independent requests may run concurrently.

questions.question: How do you prevent RxJS memory leaks?
questions.answer: Prefer async pipe or lifecycle-aware cleanup, and ensure long-lived subscriptions have an explicit owner.
questions.example: A component can use takeUntilDestroyed for a subscription tied to its lifetime.
questions.followup: What happens to a stream that never completes?

questions.question: A list of 10,000 rows is slow. What do you do?
questions.answer: Measure rendering and data costs, use stable tracking, virtual scrolling where appropriate, pagination, lazy data and efficient change detection.
questions.example: Use @for with a stable item id and virtualize a truly large viewport.
questions.followup: How do you prove the bottleneck is rendering?

questions.question: How would you structure a large Angular application?
questions.answer: Separate feature boundaries, shared UI primitives, core infrastructure and state ownership; keep components focused and APIs typed.
questions.example: A feature owns its routes and services while shared contains reusable presentational components.
questions.followup: When is a global store unnecessary?

questions.question: How would you migrate AngularJS to Angular?
questions.answer: Establish tests and boundaries, migrate feature-by-feature, isolate legacy APIs and progressively remove framework coupling.
questions.example: Move one workflow from controller/$scope to a standalone Angular feature while retaining a stable backend contract.
questions.followup: How do you reduce migration risk?
